items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: I used to play in a rhythm & blues band called the Danny Wright Orchestra. And Danny Wright’s band had an interesting rhythm section. It actually had ... a wonderful pianist named Carl Schroeder

ctx.x: Okay. It got to a point at Berklee where, did you feel like I’m ready to get out and play? Well let me rephrase that. Did you get out and play, like with Johnny Hammond, before you felt you were ready?

I think I was — I was nervous about it and I was still in school when I was playing with Johnny Hammond. I mean I might have been in my third year, I mean, and I got recommended to Johnny Hammond through — I used to play in a rhythm & blues band called the Danny Wright Orchestra. And Danny Wright’s band had an interesting rhythm section. It actually had a drummer that became my drummer years later, Peter Donald, who lives in California, a wonderful pianist named Carl Schroeder, who is a mad scientist who teaches…

Morley, you know. It wasn’t important. But that’s where we played seven nights a week and a matinee on Sunday. And you’d play like three or four sets a night. You know you’d play ‘till like two in the morning, and you’d get up and go to school. And it was at that point where I realized I really wanted to be a player. I was out playing professionally then, and playing with people that had nothing to do with the school, a guy that wouldn’t know one mode from the other, could care less how much you knew. All he just…
